reason: Combining the Sun with its disk seems a useful starting point for understanding the temperature differences between orbits.
expectation: I expect the Sun to heat the disk unevenly, though I’m unsure what item this produces.

alternatives.reason: Heating icy dust might advance the inner-disk goal, but I’d first like to establish the disk’s temperature structure.

effect: The inner disk is heated by both sunlight and accretion, setting up a distinction between materials that can remain solid at different distances.
reaction: That temperature distinction makes the next steps feel purposeful.
reason: Putting icy dust in hot inner orbits should show what happens to its ice and advance the inner-disk goal.
expectation: I expect the ice to vaporize, leaving rocky dust, though the resulting item is uncertain.

alternatives.reason: Further developing the hot inner region also seems relevant, but the ice offers a more concrete test of the heating.

effect: The ice sublimates into water vapor in warm orbits; the result does not mention leftover rocky dust.
reaction: It is useful to see that the water remains present even when the ice cannot.
reason: Moving the vapor to cold outer orbits seems relevant to storing ice beyond the snow line.
expectation: I expect the water to freeze or deposit as ice in the colder region, though I’m unsure of the resulting item.

alternatives.reason: Developing the hot inner region could advance the rocky-mixture goal, but I want to follow the water first.

effect: Water vapor can move outward and condense again, so the disk processes inherited water rather than merely storing it.
reaction: Following the water through heating and cooling is satisfying.
reason: Combining the recondensed ice with icy dust seems the direct next step toward storing outer-disk ice.
expectation: I expect an ice-rich collection of outer-disk solids, though I’m unsure whether that completes the goal.

alternatives.reason: The hot inner region remains relevant to the rocky-mixture goal, but I want to finish following the ice first.

effect: The outer-disk ice store combines inherited and reprocessed ice with dust, completing that goal; the rocky mixture remains.
reaction: It is satisfying to see the two sources of ice brought together.
reason: This is the only offered combination and should advance the remaining inner-disk goal.
expectation: I expect it to develop the hot inner region, though I’m unsure what it produces.

effect: The hottest inner-disk region evaporates inherited grains, so the rocky material must be reprocessed from vapor.
reaction: I’m curious how the vapor becomes solid again.
reason: This is the only offered combination and may let the vapor cool toward forming rocky material.
expectation: I expect the vapor to cool in open space, possibly allowing solids to condense, though the result is uncertain.

effect: Cooling the vapor produced refractory mineral grains, providing solids for the inner-disk mixture.
reaction: It's satisfying to see solids condense again after the grains evaporated.
reason: This is the only offered combination and directly combines the new minerals with rock-forming dust.
expectation: I expect a rocky inner-disk mixture, though it may need further processing.

effect: The refractory grains and rock-forming dust form a loose aggregate containing grains with different histories.
reaction: The mixed origins are an interesting detail.
reason: This is the only offered combination and may further process the rocky aggregate.
expectation: I expect the brief heating to melt or alter some of the grains, though I’m unsure what it produces.

effect: Brief heating melted some solids into droplets, while the heating mechanism remains unspecified.
reaction: The distinction between the observed melting and its disputed cause is useful.
reason: This is the only offered combination and should help the molten droplets cool.
expectation: I expect the droplets to cool and solidify, though I’m unsure what they will become.

effect: The droplets solidified into chondrules whose textures preserve evidence of rapid heating and cooling.
reaction: It is interesting that the cooled particles retain a record of their formation.
reason: This is the only offered combination and should bring metal into the rocky mixture.
expectation: I expect a mixture of chondrules and metal grains, possibly completing the inner-disk goal.

effect: The chondrules and metal became a rocky-body ingredient mixture, completing the remaining goal without yet forming a planet.
reaction: The distinction between assembled ingredients and an actual planet is useful.

mostWorthwhile.text: Following water from warm-orbit vapor to recondensed outer-disk ice was satisfying and made the disk’s processing of water clear.

leastWorthwhile.text: The run of only-offered combinations on the inner-disk path was informative but offered little meaningful choice.

surprise.text: Cooled chondrules retain textural evidence of rapid heating and cooling, even though the heating mechanism remains disputed.

arbitrary.text: Using open space to cool the hot vapor felt somewhat abstract, although the resulting condensation had a clear purpose.

continue.text: Yes. I’d be curious to see how the ice and rocky mixture become larger bodies, especially after learning how differently their materials were processed.
